contract: A team event whose hosts are split into always-present (fixed) hosts and a rotating (round-robin) pool must not be accepted unless BOTH conditions hold at the requested time: every fixed host is available AND at least one host from the rotating pool has actually been assigned. The check must run before the booking is persisted, and any failure must be reported with an error code that names which of the two conditions was unmet, carried unchanged through every layer that translates booking errors into a caller-facing message (the error-code enum, the i18n catalogue, and each API version's error translator), so the caller learns whether the fixed hosts or the rotating pool was the blocker.

defect_location.summary: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:806-901 splits the available users into fixedUserPool and luckyUserPool and then enforces only half the contract: lines 896-899 assert 'ALL fixed users must be available' and throw ErrorCode.HostsUnavailableForBooking, but there is no symmetric assertion that a rotating host was picked. The while loop at 827-895 can exit with luckyUsers empty (break at 832 when freeUsers runs out, at 854-856 when getLuckyUser returns nothing, or via the catch at 886-891 that pushes every candidate into notAvailableLuckyUsers), and line 901 then sets users = [...fixedUserPool, ...luckyUsers] with the fixed hosts alone, so the booking is created and only falls over downstream. The same one-sided rule appears in the recurring pre-check at handleNewBooking.ts:724-738, whose comment says 'each fixed user must be available' and which iterates only fixedUsers, never a rotating host. The availability gate it calls, packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking/ensureAvailableUsers.ts:213-252, accumulates availableUsers without regard to user.isFixed and at 249-252 throws a single undifferentiated Error(ErrorCode.NoAvailableUsersFound), so no caller can tell the two failure modes apart; it is also the file that would have to return or raise the fixed-vs-rotating distinction. packages/lib/errorCodes.ts:1-25 lists NoAvailableUsersFound and HostsUnavailableForBooking but no code for 'no rotating host available', and because these enum values are i18n keys (apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json:118 maps 'hosts_unavailable_for_booking' to its message) a new condition needs an entry there too. apps/api/v2/src/ee/bookings/2024-08-13/services/errors.service.ts:34-53 is where the loss becomes the reported symptom: 'no_available_users_found_error' and 'hosts_unavailable_for_booking' both collapse into the blanket BadRequestException 'One of the hosts either already has booking at this time or is not available', and anything unrecognised is rethrown raw at line 53. packages/features/bookings/Booker/components/hooks/useBookings.ts:18,295 is the client-side counterpart that special-cases individual ErrorCode values and would need the new one. packages/lib/server/getLuckyUser.ts is the rotation resolver whose empty result the missing guard fails to detect.
